text.summary: Dunmere's acting head, practical and overburdened.
text.full: The acting head of Dunmere. Practical, tired, and under too much pressure to entertain theories that do not quickly become useful.

schedule.activity_text: The innkeeper wipes down tables near the hearth before road traffic gathers.
The innkeeper moves between tables, keeping one eye on the door.
The innkeeper moves between tables, keeping one eye on the door.
The innkeeper has withdrawn from the common room for the night.

text.summary: The innkeeper, observant and more worried than he wants to sound.
text.full: Owner of the Grey Road Inn. Friendly enough to talk, observant enough to notice patterns, and worried enough to measure every rumor against the next one.

schedule.activity_text: A shaken woman sits near the hearth, both hands tight around a torn caravan sash.
A shaken woman grips a torn caravan sash near the fire and watches every door too quickly.
A shaken survivor sits apart from the common room, trying to hold a memory still long enough to speak it.

text.summary: A shaken traveler whose memory keeps slipping at the worst moments.
text.full: A survivor of one of the Grey Road attacks. She remembers enough to know something was wrong, but not enough to trust memory without help.

schedule.activity_text: Travelers keep their voices low, watching each new arrival before returning to their cups.
Travelers gather in small knots, their conversations dropping whenever the road outside creaks.
Only a few travelers remain awake, speaking quietly near the last warm coals.

text.summary: Travelers and patrons who carry rumor, caution, and half-finished stories.
text.full: A shifting group of road-worn travelers and local patrons. None of them owns the mystery, but many have brushed against its consequences.

text.summary: A reclusive hunter who knows the old paths better than most people in Dunmere.
text.full: A quiet, defensive hunter who knows the forest paths and resents being treated like a suspect simply because he sees more than others do.

text.summary: Leader of the bandits near the shrine, volatile and visibly strained.
text.full: Leader of a small bandit group using the ruined shrine as a base. He is dangerous in his own right, but also reacting to pressure he does not understand.

text.summary: A nervous bandit who makes the shrine more dangerous only when scaling explicitly permits it.
text.full: A lesser bandit drawn into Rusk's orbit. They add pressure for a larger party, but are not important enough to change the story's center of gravity.

text.summary: A villager whose brother is missing and whose fear is turning into certainty.
text.full: A determined villager whose missing brother has left her desperate for answers and increasingly suspicious of everyone around her.

text.summary: An unseen influence beneath the shrine that presses on thought instead of flesh.
text.full: A subtle, persuasive influence anchored beneath the ruined shrine. It does not command in words so much as bend attention, coordination, and certainty.
